verdict.rationale: Linear's Loops let users describe a recurring job in plain language and run it via Linear Agent on a schedule or in response to workspace events. Examples include changes to initiatives, projects and cycles, which can trigger document updates and Slack posts without manual intervention. Coding sessions also run in the cloud, but the evidence is changelog-level only, and the older community complaint about weak workflow automation predates Loops. Missing for 10: in-depth documentation of loop configuration, limits and monitoring; independent hands-on corroboration of loops running autonomously.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can set up automations that run autonomously in the background

citations.quote: Loops are a new way for Linear Agent to take on recurring work for your team. Describe the job in plain language and then choose whether it should run on a schedule or in response to an event.
Loops are recurring agent workflows for teams. They now respond to more workspace activity, including changes to initiatives, projects, and cycles.
When a project's target date changes, a loop can automatically update the launch plan and post a Slack message explaining what changed, why, and who needs to act.
Coding sessions run in the cloud, so you can prototype ideas and make changes without setting up a local development environment.
